reason: This is exactly my pain: we just repeated an outage we'd already written a postmortem for, and agents briefed on prior incidents would have caught it. But I'm not handing Slack, Drive and GitHub to a hosted product in early preview from a company I've never heard of. This month I'd have someone self-host it on a couple of repos, not pay for seats.
objection: Will this company still exist in two years, and can I trust an early-preview cloud with our incident history and internal Slack? MIT licence means I'm not stranded, but then I'm the one running it and keeping it alive.
would_change_my_mind: A self-hosted pilot where it actually flags the incident we repeated, from our own postmortem, before an agent touches that code, plus a SOC 2 report or a named reference customer my size on the paid cloud.
